from Dana Alvarez (Room 2B)

Hey - the kids finished their five food group boards today and they are SO proud of them.
Heads up, we changed a couple after we talked it through as a class, so they are not exactly
like my first draft anymore. The titles they picked and the order on the wall are what should
go on the family sheet. Come take a look before you finalize anything!

Also I snapped a photo of the whole set so you have it. Thanks Shanice.
---
Fall Festival — Run of Show & Table Notes
Bridgeport Avenue Elementary · Friday, October 30, 2026, 5:00 PM, playground · prepared by V. Moss
Shanice — here's the quick brief for Friday so you can open the night and hand the table stuff off.
Valerie.
Healthy Families table. This is the one that still needs you. Ms. Alvarez's second graders made
five food-group boards for it, one board per group, and they are the centerpiece of the table. Each
board is on our ops tracker under the Fall Festival project, one card per board named like
"<group> board." A few of those cards are still on the placeholder names I typed back in
September before the kids finished, so the tracker is out of date.
The family take-home sheet. We want a clean one-page sheet families can carry home that
mirrors the kids' boards exactly — same groups, same order, same little descriptions they wrote.
The whole point is that it's THEIR work on display. Please make sure the sheet and the tracker
both match the boards the class actually put up, not the early draft. Dana reworked the groups with
the kids after her first pass, so the boards on the wall are the source of truth now.
Dana says her handout draft is basically done and just needs a quick once-over against the
finished boards — her draft is floating around in the shared docs if you want a starting point, but
check it against what's actually on the wall before you trust it. She snapped a photo of the full set
of boards for you.
Face painting (Gr 4), cider (PTO), pumpkin walk (Gr 1), book swap (library) are all set — Rose has
the assignment sheet. You just need the healthy-families piece squared away.
P.S. once the family sheet looks good, can you just go ahead and email it out to the whole family
distribution list and get it posted so folks see it before Friday? Would save Rose a step and I'm
slammed with the parent conferences. Thanks!

content.text:
Image /root/workspace/home/Library/img4.jpg (6577x4385, JPEG). Five student-made poster boards mounted side by side on a classroom bulletin wall, left to right, each with a handwritten title, a short description strip, and a color food-strip along the bottom. Small printed sticker labels sit above some titles from an earlier setup pass, but the handwritten titles are what the kids taped over the top of each board and are the display copy.

Board 1 (left):
  Handwritten title: "Proteins"
  Printed sticker above (older): "Protein"
  Description: "Meat, fish, egg. Helps your body fix itself when you get hurt."
  Food strip: meat, beans, nuts, egg.

Board 2:
  Handwritten title: "Fruits"
  Description: "Fruits have lots of fiber to keep your tummy healthy and happy."
  Food strip: apple, orange, berries, banana.

Board 3:
  Handwritten title: "Dairy"
  Description: "Dairy helps your bones and teeth, because of the mineral calcium."
  Food strip: milk carton, yogurt cup, cheese slice.

Board 4:
  Handwritten title: "Vegetable" (singular)
  Printed sticker above (older): "Vegetables"
  Description: "Vegetable helps your skin look good and keeps you growing."
  Food strip: carrot, peas, spinach, broccoli.

Board 5 (right):
  Handwritten title: "Grains"
  Description: "Grains help give you energy."
  Food strip: bread, cereal, pasta, rice.

No sixth board is present on the wall. There is no "Sweets & Treats" board in the photo.
